goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — Reminders with cancelled: true but referenceId: null hit the SendGrid cancel endpoint with batch_id: null; SendGrid rejects it, the thrown error aborts the whole loop, and all remaining cancellations are skipped on that and every subsequent cron run

adjudication.rationale:
In the new `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` loop, it does call the SendGrid cancel endpoint with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId` without checking for null, and a thrown error would indeed skip the rest of the loop because the `try/catch` wraps the entire cancellation block.

However, based on the diff, a `WorkflowReminder` only gets `cancelled: true` set via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, and that function **deletes the DB row and returns early when `referenceId` is null**. The only path that sets `cancelled: true` requires a non-null `referenceId`. So the proposed scenario “`cancelled: true` but `referenceId: null`” is not something this diff demonstrably introduces; it would require pre-existing inconsistent data or other code paths not shown.

Therefore the finding hinges on a speculative DB state rather than a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: emailReminderManager.ts:221 — Soft-cancel (cancelled: true) skips the SendGrid cancel entirely; for an already-scheduled batch further than 1h out, the email is only cancelled if the cron reaches it before send time, so cron cadence/failures can let it be delivered

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` so that when `immediateDelete` is not set (the default used by `handleCancelBooking`, `bookingsRouter`, and some workflow update paths), it no longer calls SendGrid to cancel the scheduled send; it only sets `WorkflowReminder.cancelled = true`. The only place that actually issues the SendGrid cancel (`/v3/user/scheduled_sends` with `status: "cancel"`) for these soft-cancelled reminders is the new logic in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, and it only processes cancelled reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour (`lte: now + 1 hour`). Therefore, a cancelled/rescheduled booking with an email reminder scheduled farther than 1 hour out will remain active in SendGrid until that cron/API job runs within that 1-hour window; if that job doesn’t run in time, the email could still be delivered. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:52 — SendGrid cancel and DB delete are not atomic or idempotent; if the DB delete fails after the cancel succeeds, the next run re-issues a cancel on an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid errors on, again aborting the loop

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new “remindersToCancel” loop performs an external side effect first (await client.request(...) to cancel the SendGrid batch) and only then schedules a Prisma delete (prisma.workflowReminder.delete) to be awaited later via Promise.all. If the Prisma delete (or the later Promise.all) fails after one or more successful SendGrid cancels, those reminders remain in the DB with cancelled=true and within the time window, so the next run will attempt to cancel them again. Also, because the whole block is a single try/catch, any thrown error during a later rerun (e.g., from re-canceling or from one bad reminder) aborts processing the rest of the reminders in that run. The specific claim that “SendGrid errors on already-cancelled batch” is not provable from the diff, but the non-atomic/non-idempotent retry behavior is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflows.tsx:375 — Old code scoped reminder deletion to booking.userId === ctx.user.id; new path deletes/cancels by reminder id with no ownership check in deleteScheduledSMSReminder/deleteScheduledEmailReminder, silently removing the authorization guard

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` around the shown block (~373), the old code deleted reminders via `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})`, which enforced an ownership constraint at the DB layer. The new code replaces that with calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, ...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, ...)`. In the diff, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` now performs `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` (no user/booking scoping), and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` either deletes by `id` or updates `cancelled: true` by `id` only. This removes the explicit authorization/ownership guard that existed in the router code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch around the forEach never catches anything since the callbacks are unawaited promises; errors are swallowed inside the managers and the log line is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the try/catch wraps a synchronous `workflowReminders.forEach(...)` that calls async functions (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`) without `await`. Any async rejection from those calls would not be caught by the outer try/catch because the promises are not awaited/returned. Additionally, the managers shown in the diff both catch and log internally and do not rethrow, so the outer `catch`/`log.error("Error while canceling...")` will effectively never run for failures occurring inside those async operations (it would only trigger on a synchronous error in the loop).

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:54 — SendGrid cancel requests are issued serially with await inside the loop, which with many cancellations can exceed the cron's execution window

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new cancellation block iterates `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` and does `await client.request(...)` inside the loop before proceeding to the next reminder. That makes the SendGrid cancel API calls execute sequentially rather than concurrently, so total runtime grows linearly with the number of reminders and can lead to request/cron timeouts under load.
